name: Industrial digital twins
summary: Living digital models connect engineering designs and operational data so organizations can simulate, monitor and improve physical assets.
useCase: A manufacturer tests a proposed production-line change in a synchronized model before moving equipment or changing control software.
whyNow: Engineering software, simulation and industrial data platforms are converging. The World Economic Forum’s Global Lighthouse Network expanded from 90 recognized advanced-manufacturing sites in 2021 to 223 in early 2026. That is an adjacent indicator of advanced operational technology, not a digital-twin census. Useful twins require continuing data synchronization and a decision they can improve; a static 3D model alone is insufficient.

mainstream.scope: Synchronized operational twins used routinely for high-value manufacturing, infrastructure and energy assets.
mainstream.rationale: Long asset lives and existing engineering platforms provide a strong distribution route, while simulation can reduce commissioning and operating risk. Adoption is likely to concentrate where errors are expensive and data is available. The window assumes model-maintenance costs and interoperability improve; universal twins of every factory are not assumed.

direction: Expanding from design into live operations

metric.name: Global Lighthouse Network sites — adjacent Industry 4.0 proxy
metric.scope: WEF-selected advanced-manufacturing lighthouses; a recognition network, not all digital-twin deployments.
metric.limitations: Selective recognition of many Industry 4.0 technologies. Not every site uses a digital twin, and many unrecognized sites do. Selection pace and dates differ; no market-size or adoption-rate CAGR should be inferred.
metric.futureNote: No reliable same-definition future site count is supplied. The analyst scenario concerns operational digital twins, while the historical proxy measures broader advanced manufacturing.

maturity.note: Analyst ordinal assessment, not an adoption percentage: 0 research, 1 proof of concept, 2 pilots, 3 commercial niche, 4 routine use in the stated market, 5 established/expanding. Future values are a scenario.

milestones.text: The Global Lighthouse Network reached 90 recognized advanced-manufacturing sites.
Siemens and NVIDIA announced a partnership linking industrial software and real-time simulation.
No comparable annual digital-twin deployment census identified; adjacent-site recognition is not substituted as adoption.
The lighthouse network reached 189 sites in January.
The network reached 223 sites; Schneider agreed to acquire PTC, with closing expected in Q3 2027.

tailwinds: Simulation can lower commissioning costs and test expensive changes before implementation.
Equipment, engineering and operational software vendors already serve the target customers.
bottlenecks: Models become stale unless asset configuration and sensor data remain synchronized.
Interoperability, ownership of data and ongoing maintenance can outweigh the initial visualization benefit.
watchMetrics: Number of production assets with regularly synchronized, decision-used twins.
Measured commissioning time, downtime, energy or quality improvement against a baseline; include model upkeep costs.
